subject: Physical Education, Sport and Mass Displays
curriculum: Zimbabwe Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (MoPSE) - Junior (Grade 3-7)
syllabus_source: Physical Education, Sport and Mass Displays Junior School Level Teacher's Guide, Grade 3-7, 2015-2022 - official MoPSE document, fetched and verified directly, including the full Scope and Sequence Chart
confidence_flag: This file is grounded directly in the official Teacher's Guide, which was retrieved in full including its complete Scope and Sequence Chart covering all 3 Study Areas (Physical Education, Sport, Mass Displays) across all their topics and sub-topics for Grade 3-7. This is the most thoroughly verified file in the collection - essentially the entire official grade-by-grade content matrix was captured.

chunks.strand: Syllabus Overview
chunks.topic: Rationale and Structure
chunks.content: Physical Education, Sport and Mass Displays (PESMD) plays a leading role in the total development of the learner, serving as the primary means through which learners acquire knowledge, skills, right attitudes and values across the curriculum, in pursuit of a lifelong physically active and healthy lifestyle. It ensures access regardless of gender, race, religion, handicap or current participation level, promotes psychomotor skill development, and ensures learners develop physically, mentally, socially, emotionally and morally, while gaining aesthetic awareness. Safety is stated as a pre-requisite for all PESMD activities.

chunks.strand: Syllabus Overview
chunks.topic: The 3 Study Areas
chunks.content: The syllabus is organised into 3 Study Areas: Study Area 1 - Physical Education (Human Body, Safety and Health, Aquatic Skills, Kids Athletics); Study Area 2 - Sport/Game Skills (Invasion Games, Net Games, Striking Games, Target and Combat Games, Adventure Games, Educational Gymnastics); and Study Area 3 - Mass Displays (Music, Background Art, Arena Acts).

chunks.strand: Syllabus Overview
chunks.topic: Aims of the Learning Area
chunks.content: The syllabus aims to: develop organic health and fitness for all learners; provide children with a sense of achievement and enjoyment; develop individual skills and competences; develop character traits such as will power, determination, self-discipline and a spirit of co-operation; and foster a body of knowledge specifically relating to sports.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Human Body
chunks.topic: Organs of the Body - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Humans have external and internal body parts. Grade 4: Humans have external and internal body parts with different functions. Grade 5: Humans have body parts that store and transport food. Grade 6: Humans have external and internal parts with functions in storing and transporting food and air. Grade 7: Humans have body parts that store and transport food, air and blood.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Human Body
chunks.topic: Human Body - Grade 3 Worked Lesson Example
chunks.content: A verified Grade 3 lesson on the human body has learners identify and name parts of the human body and differentiate between males and females, covering different parts and external/internal parts of the human body. Note: the guide explicitly states 'NO naming of genitals' as a coaching point for this lesson - body-part identification stays at an age-appropriate level.
learning_activities: Singing rhymes and playing games while naming body parts, e.g. 'Head and Shoulders, Knees and Toes'
Identifying and naming parts of the human body; drawing the human body
Role playing left and right orientation
Fitting jigsaw puzzles of males and females; modelling a human body

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Safety and Health
chunks.topic: Healthy Living Habits - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Healthy living habits at home. Grade 4: Health-related fitness (endurance, strength, flexibility, body composition); healthy living habits at home and school. Grade 5: Sport-related fitness components; healthy living habits at home, school and community; safety precautions and rules in handling apparatus; warm up and cool down; diseases caused by lack of exercise. Grade 6: Healthy living habits at home, school and community; physical activity diary; diseases caused by lack of exercise, nutrition and poor sanitary conditions. Grade 7: Healthy living lifestyles; healthy living projects; injury prevention and management.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Safety and Health
chunks.topic: Safety Rules - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Safety rules for various environments; warm up and cool down. Grade 4: Safety rules and precautions for various activities. Grade 5: Safety rules when participating in physical activities; safety rules, storage and care of apparatus. Grade 6: Safety when participating in physical activities; safety precautions and rules in handling apparatus; warm up and cool down; safety rules and regulations for various activities; injuries related to various physical activities. Grade 7: Safety rules and precautions for various activities in different environments; safety rules, storage and care of apparatus.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Safety and Health
chunks.topic: Content and Objectives (General, All Grades)
chunks.content: Safety and Health content covers: safety rules in and around the playing area; safety rules with self and others; playing to keep healthy and fit; exercising to stay healthy and fit; eating healthy food; personal and environmental hygiene; and eating habits. Objectives across grades include: identifying hazardous objects in and around the environment, discussing playing area safety rules, and exercising regularly to maintain physical fitness, mental health, and enhance muscular development, strength and body coordination.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Aquatic Skills
chunks.topic: Water Safety - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Survival skills in and near water. Grade 4: Survival skills in and near water. Grade 5: Aquatic survival skills. Grade 6: Survival techniques in water; water hazards. Grade 7: Survival techniques in water; resuscitation techniques.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Aquatic Skills
chunks.topic: Swimming Strokes - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Arm and leg action; floating with or without aid; submerging; water treading; gliding; breathing. Grade 4: Floating; water treading; gliding; submerging; arm and leg action at increased intervals; entry into water. Grade 5: Floating; gliding; submerging; turning; arm and leg action; front, back and breast stroke. Grade 6: Front and back crawl techniques; breast stroke; entry into water; tumble turn. Grade 7: Front, back crawl and butterfly strokes; entry into water.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Kids Athletics
chunks.topic: Running, Jumping and Throwing - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: RUNNING: Grade 3 - progressive endurance race, slalom shuttle relays; Grade 4 - bend running and obstacle clearing with varying speed; Grade 5 - 8-minute endurance race, sprint-hurdle relays, bends formula; Grade 6 - running techniques and tactics, running with obstacles; Grade 7 - running tactics and techniques, running with obstacles. JUMPING: Grade 3 - jumping with/without equipment; Grade 4 - jumping with/without apparatus for distance and height; Grade 5 - jumping for distance; Grade 6 - jumping for height; Grade 7 - jumping for height using a pole, horizontal/vertical jumping techniques. THROWING: Grade 3 - front and backward throwing, kids javelin throw, throwing over a barrier; Grade 4 - standing throw kids javelin for distance/accuracy, throwing over a barrier for target; Grade 5 - rotational throw for distance/accuracy, target throw over a barrier; Grade 6 - teen javelin for height and distance; Grade 7 - throwing techniques.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Invasion Games
chunks.topic: Space Awareness and Positioning - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: SPACE AWARENESS: Grade 3 - open space; Grade 4 - occupied space; Grade 5 - space creation; Grade 6 - defending/attacking in relation to time and speed, running into open space, covering open space; Grade 7 - advantages/disadvantages of moving into open or closed space, defending and attacking as a team, formations. POSITIONING: Grade 3 - positioning within boundaries; Grade 4 - positioning within boundaries and teammates; Grade 5 - positioning within boundaries, teammates and opponents; Grade 6-7 - positioning within boundaries in relation to teammates and opponents. REACTION: Grade 3 - reaction into open/occupied space; Grade 4 - reaction in relation to movement; Grade 5 - defensive roles; Grade 6 - offensive roles; Grade 7 - principles of attack and defense in relation to time, dislodging an opponent.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Target and Combat Games
chunks.topic: Aiming/Targeting and Stance - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: AIMING/TARGETING: Grade 3 - target up to 15m, stationary targets; Grade 4 - stationary and slow mobile target, target up to 25m; Grade 5 - stationary and average mobile targets, target up to 35m; Grade 6 - stationary and fast mobile target for height, target up to 40m; Grade 7 - stationary and fast mobile targets for height, target up to 50m. STANCE: Grade 3 - balance on the base of support; Grade 4 - weight transfer and distribution; Grade 5 - wide and narrow base, follow through; Grade 6 - body orientation for movement, energy conversions over time; Grade 7 - energy conversions and release, adjusting body position.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Net Games
chunks.topic: Strokes and Grip - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: STROKES: Grade 3 - types of strokes; Grade 4 - strokes for speed and direction; Grade 5 - strokes for height, spin and distance; Grade 6 - strokes for height, spin, distance and power; Grade 7 - strokes for height, spin, distance and power in relation to time. GRIP: Grade 3 - correct handling of equipment; Grade 4 - grip and stance; Grade 5 - grip, stance and footwork; Grade 6 - grip, stance, footwork; Grade 7 - grip, stance, footwork, movement in striking for distance.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Striking Games
chunks.topic: Striking - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Forward drives from a stationary position. Grade 4: Forward drives from a mobile position; backward strokes/drives from a stationary position. Grade 5: Backward strokes/drives from a mobile position. Grade 6: Well-timed backward or forward drives with reaction; backward/forward strokes (footwork, co-ordination). Grade 7: Accurate backward and forward drive for space, distance and scoring.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Adventure Games
chunks.topic: Outdoor Activities - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Course marking; walking; orienteering. Grade 4: Orienteering; walking steeper gradient. Grade 5: Orienteering; mountaineering; animal riding (e.g. horses, elephants, donkeys). Grade 6: Orienteering; climbing and abseiling; cycling; water-based activities. Grade 7: Orienteering; water-based activities; mountaineering and abseiling.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Educational Gymnastics
chunks.topic: Locomotion - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Basic general balances and weight-bearing movements; moving, creating shapes and formations. Grade 4: Balancing and weight transference in relation to apparatus; balancing and creating enhanced shapes and formations. Grade 5: Basic general speed in movement using different body parts (slow, medium, fast); linking movements to develop sequences. Grade 6: Balancing and creating enhanced shapes/formations in movement (light and heavy); transference of weight using different body parts at different levels; forceful movements; sequences in movements. Grade 7: Contrasting quick, light and heavy movements; increased range of movement through exploration; improved, more complex movement sequences through practice and critical analysis.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Educational Gymnastics
chunks.topic: Balances - Worked Lesson Example
chunks.grade: General (Grade level not specified in source)
chunks.content: A worked balances lesson has learners balance on different points and transfer/bear weight, covering solo balances with moderate motor skills, basic general balances (in pairs and in groups), and balances creating shapes and formations. Balancing progresses through one point, two points, three points, four points, five points and six points of contact, plus transferring/bearing weight through balancing on each other and matching balances.
learning_activities: Balancing on one to six points progressively
Transferring and bearing weight through balancing on each other
Linking balances in pairs or groups (matching balances)

chunks.strand: Study Area 3 - Mass Displays: Music
chunks.topic: Background and Performing Music - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3: Common play and dance songs; rhythm and stimuli. Grade 4: Rhythm and stimuli; percussion band. Grade 5: Percussion band and other musical instruments; use of instruments. Grade 6: Band; recorded music. Grade 7: Use of music.

chunks.strand: Study Area 3 - Mass Displays: Background Art
chunks.topic: Patterns and Mounts - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: Grade 3-4: Letters and pictures related to portrayed themes. Grade 5: Shapes, colours and symbols depicting themes. Grade 6: Shapes, pictures, colours and symbols describing themes. Grade 7: Shapes, pictures and symbols describing themes on display, mounted on sets of boards and books.

chunks.strand: Study Area 3 - Mass Displays: Arena Arts
chunks.topic: Movement, Rhythm and Choreography - Verified Grade 3-7 Scope and Sequence
chunks.content: MOVEMENT AND RHYTHM: Grade 3 - rhythmic movement to cover space/direction without tempo; Grade 4 - rhythmic movement to cover space/direction for play themes; Grade 5 - rhythmic movement with tempo for play and traditional game themes; Grade 6 - rhythmic movement with variations using educational themes; Grade 7 - movement covering space/direction with varying rhythms using complex themes. CHOREOGRAPHY: progresses from calculated movement into the arena and rhythmic choreography (Grade 3-4), through combining movement with routines from play/sport themes (Grade 5), to combined movement and choreography with complex formations by Grade 7.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Safety and Health
chunks.topic: Components of Fitness Explained
chunks.content: Health-related fitness has four main components: endurance (the ability to sustain physical activity over a period of time without tiring, e.g. running long distances - also called cardiovascular/aerobic fitness), strength (the amount of force a muscle or muscle group can produce, e.g. lifting or pushing something heavy), flexibility (the range of motion available at a joint, e.g. being able to touch your toes), and body composition (the ratio of fat to lean mass - muscle, bone, organs - in the body). Sport-related fitness adds further components relevant to specific sports, such as speed, agility (the ability to change direction quickly while controlling the body), power (a combination of strength and speed), balance, coordination, and reaction time. Regular exercise, a balanced diet and adequate rest all contribute to developing and maintaining these fitness components.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Safety and Health
chunks.topic: Why Warm Up and Cool Down Matter
chunks.content: A warm-up is light physical activity performed before the main exercise session, typically including gentle cardiovascular movement (e.g. light jogging) followed by dynamic stretching. It gradually raises heart rate, increases blood flow to muscles, raises muscle temperature, and prepares joints for a fuller range of motion - all of which reduce the risk of injury (such as muscle strains) during the main activity and improve performance. A cool-down is light activity performed after exercise, typically including slower movement (e.g. walking) followed by static stretching (holding a stretch without movement). It helps gradually lower the heart rate back to resting levels, helps remove waste products (like lactic acid) from muscles, and reduces post-exercise muscle stiffness and soreness. Skipping either can increase injury risk and slow recovery.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Aquatic Skills
chunks.topic: Basic Swimming Strokes Explained
chunks.content: Front crawl (freestyle) is the fastest common stroke: the swimmer lies face-down, alternating overarm arm movements (pulling through the water then recovering above the surface) with a continuous flutter kick, and turns the head to the side to breathe. Backstroke is swum on the back with an alternating overarm arm action (mirroring front crawl but on the back) and a flutter kick, allowing the swimmer to breathe freely since the face stays above water. Breaststroke involves a simultaneous, symmetrical arm pull (a sweeping outward-then-inward motion) combined with a frog-like whip kick, and the head lifts forward to breathe - it is typically the slowest of the competitive strokes but often the first taught for its stability. Butterfly is the most physically demanding stroke, using a simultaneous, symmetrical overarm arm recovery combined with a dolphin kick (both legs moving together in an undulating motion) and is usually the last stroke introduced (by Grade 7 in this syllabus) once foundational strokes and water confidence are established.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Aquatic Skills
chunks.topic: Basic Water Safety and Survival Skills
chunks.content: Basic water survival skills include: floating (relaxing the body face-up or face-down to stay at the surface with minimal effort, conserving energy), treading water (using small, continuous arm and leg movements to keep the head above water while stationary), and controlled breathing (timing breaths with strokes or floating position to avoid inhaling water). Water safety rules include: never swimming alone, always swimming in supervised or designated safe areas, entering unfamiliar water feet-first rather than diving to check depth and check for hazards, and knowing basic rescue priorities - in an emergency, reaching or throwing something to a struggling swimmer (a pole, rope, or floating object) is safer than jumping in to physically grab them, since a panicking swimmer can accidentally pull a rescuer under.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Invasion Games
chunks.topic: What 'Invasion Games' Means and Example Sports
chunks.content: Invasion games are team sports where the objective is to move into an opponent's territory to score, while defending your own goal/territory - examples include football/soccer, netball, basketball, rugby, and hockey. Core tactical principles shared across invasion games include: creating and using space (moving to open areas to receive the ball and make play easier), maintaining good positioning relative to teammates and opponents, quick reaction/decision-making, and switching between attacking (trying to score) and defending (trying to stop the opposition scoring) roles as possession of the ball/object changes. These principles are taught progressively and generically across grades so learners can transfer tactical understanding between different invasion sports, not just master one specific game.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Net Games
chunks.topic: What 'Net Games' Means and Example Sports
chunks.content: Net games are sports where players/teams are separated by a net and aim to hit or strike an object (ball or shuttlecock) into the opponent's area in a way they cannot successfully return - examples include volleyball, tennis, badminton, and table tennis. Core skills shared across net games include: grip (how the hand holds the racket/paddle, affecting control and power), stance (body positioning for readiness and balance), footwork (moving efficiently to reach the ball/shuttle), and strokes (the striking action itself, varying in direction, height, spin and power depending on the tactical situation).

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Target and Combat Games
chunks.topic: What 'Target and Combat Games' Means and Example Activities
chunks.content: Target games involve aiming an object at a specific target to score points, with accuracy being more important than power - examples include archery, darts, bowls, and boccia. Combat games/sports involve direct physical contest between two opponents within agreed rules - examples include wrestling and judo-style grappling activities adapted for the school setting. Both categories develop precision, focus, controlled body movement, and (for combat activities) respect for rules and an opponent's safety, since these activities carry higher physical risk than most other game categories and require strict adherence to safety rules.

chunks.strand: Study Area 1 - Physical Education: Kids Athletics
chunks.topic: Athletics Events Explained
chunks.content: Kids Athletics adapts standard track and field events for younger learners. Running events range from short sprints (testing speed) to longer endurance races (testing stamina), plus relay races (a team event where a baton or object is passed between runners) and hurdle events (running while clearing obstacles at intervals). Jumping events include long jump/distance jumps (jumping horizontally for maximum distance, typically from a running approach) and high jump (jumping vertically to clear a bar at increasing heights). Throwing events include javelin (throwing a spear-like implement for distance, with a kids' version using a lighter, safer implement) and other implement throws for distance and/or accuracy. These events build foundational movement skills (running, jumping, throwing) that transfer to many other sports.

chunks.strand: Study Area 3 - Mass Displays
chunks.topic: What Mass Displays Are and Why They're Taught
chunks.content: Mass displays are large-group, choreographed performances combining rhythmic movement, music and formation patterns, typically performed at events like independence celebrations, school galas, and national ceremonies in Zimbabwe. They are built from three combined elements: Music (rhythm, percussion, songs that guide the movement), Background Art (visual elements like themed patterns, colours, letters and pictures displayed as a backdrop, often held up by a group of learners forming a 'card display'), and Arena Arts (the performers' own choreographed movement, formations, and thematic routines performed in the display space). Mass displays develop teamwork, discipline, timing, spatial awareness, and cultural/national pride, since routines often symbolise national themes, historical events, or cultural heritage.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport
chunks.topic: Indigenous Games of Zimbabwe
chunks.content: Indigenous games (mitambo yechivanhu) are traditional games passed down through generations, often played in the evening or during leisure time. Examples include: (1) Nhodo - a game involving throwing a stone into the air and picking others from a hole before catching it. (2) Pada - a jumping game played on a grid drawn on the ground. (3) Tsoro - a strategic board game using stones or seeds in holes (e.g. tsoro yemagari, tsoro yemabwe). (4) Kudoora - a game of throwing stones to hit a target. (5) Matsvaire - a tag-like game. These games develop motor skills, coordination, strategic thinking, and social values like fair play and cooperation, and are a vital part of Zimbabwean cultural heritage.

chunks.strand: Study Area 2 - Sport: Adventure Games
chunks.topic: Orienteering Explained
chunks.content: Orienteering is an outdoor activity combining navigation and physical activity: participants use a map (and sometimes a compass) to find their way to a series of marked control points in a set order, usually in unfamiliar terrain, aiming to complete the course as accurately and/or quickly as possible. It develops map-reading skills, decision-making under time pressure, problem-solving, and physical endurance (since it usually involves walking, jogging or running across varied terrain). It connects directly to the direction/compass point skills taught in English Language (Grade 6) and to broader spatial reasoning skills.
